# CT-1 — IRI generated by TARQL does not match the concept IRI

The smallest data that answers this competency question, and one command that
runs it.

```bash
./run.sh          # verdict only
./run.sh --show   # verdict plus every finding
```

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `ontologies/water.ttl` | two classes, `:Site` and `:Asset`, declared and nothing more |
| `queries/sites.rq` | the reference mapping — both templates as agreed |
| `queries/readings.rq` | the second domain — one template matches, one drifted |
| `out/` | what the run writes; `--reports minimal` keeps it to `findings.txt` (for a person) and `full_results.csv` (for this script) |

## The two sets

Each query carries both halves, in the same file, in the same style, by the
same author. The only difference between them is the thing under test.

| | Variable | sites.rq | readings.rq | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **error** | `?site_IRI` | `CONCAT("…/site-", ?siteid)` | `CONCAT("…/site-", REPLACE(?siteid," ","_"))` | **reported** |
| **control** | `?asset_IRI` | `CONCAT("…/asset-", ?assetid)` | identical, character for character | **silent** |

The error case is a real defect and not a stylistic one: for any site id
containing a space the two domains mint different IRIs for one site, and their
data never joins. Neither query is wrong read on its own — only the pair is,
which is why nothing that reads one file at a time can find it.

The control is there because a check that reported both would be useless in
exactly the way that matters, and one that reported neither would look
identical to a clean project. `run.sh` asserts both directions, so the fixture
tests whether the check *discriminates* rather than whether it fires.

## What the run should report

One finding, and it is the one under test:

| Check | Focus | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `TQL-001` | `?site_IRI` | **the point of the fixture** |

`run.sh` fails if `TQL-001` is missing for `?site_IRI`, if it appears for
`?asset_IRI`, or if *anything else* is reported at all — its allowlist is
empty and meant to stay that way.

It held one entry until suite 0.20.0. `CNF-002` fired on `:isRepresentedBy`,
a predicate in neither query: the sketch writes its namespace legend with the
CURIE `:isRepresentedBy`, and `:` means the tool's scratch namespace only
when no query declares an empty prefix. Most queries declare one, so the
tool's own predicate landed in this model's namespace and was reported as a
property nobody had declared — and nothing the project could change would
have made it go away. Fixed upstream rather than allowed for here, which is
the right disposal for any finding that turns out to be about the tool.

## What was left out, and why

Everything that produced a finding of its own, so that only the competency
under test is present or absent:

- `rdfs:subClassOf owl:Thing` — makes `owl:Thing` a declared class nothing
  populates (`CNF-005`)
- a `:siteName` property filled from a CSV column — an unbound CONSTRUCT
  variable is reported (`TQL-003`), correctly, and has nothing to do with CT-1
- any second defect of any kind — the fault is one thing, in one place
